To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel naphthoquione antibiotic was isolated from the culture filtrate and the mycelium of Streptomycetes tendae Tü901/8c.

The new juglomycin Z ( 1), which was identified by HPLC-diodes array screening, differs from all other juglomycin-type compounds by an additional methoxy group at position 3 in the naphthoqinone ring system.
the new antibiotic juglomycin Z is a new juglomycin derivative with an additional methyl group and that it is active against Gram-positive as well as Gram-negative bacteria and yeasts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of new bioactive natural products from microorganisms.
the development and the application of a HPLC-DAD screening system for the detection of naphtho- and naphtalenequinone antibiotics in actinomycete cultures.
the development of a new screening technique for the discovery of novel bioactive compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the biosynthetic origin of the juglomycin-type antibiotics can be explained by an oxidative coupling reaction of a naphthoic acid derivative and 2,3,5,6-tetrahydroxynaphthalene, which is derived from shikimic acid.
the new compound 1 represents the first naturally occurring naphthoquinoic acid with an additional substituent in the aromatic ring system.
juglomycin Z (compound 1), the new antibiotic from S. tendae Tü901/8c, is the first member of a new subgroup within the group of the juglomycins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the screening of the actinomycete collection of the DSMZ with the HPLC-DAD screening method resulted in the identification of 15 new compounds.
the biosynthesis of the naphthalene ring system of the juglomycin-type antibiotics is initiated from 1,3-dihydroxyacetone phosphate and 1-deoxy-d-xylulose-5-phosphate.
we have developed an efficient method for the detection and identification of new natural products from actinomycete cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthetic potential of actinomcyetes is far greater than previously appreciated.
the biosynthetic machinery for juglomycin biosynthesis is present in a number of actinomcetes and can be induced by the presence of a juglomycin precursor.
the actinomycete Streptomyces coelicolor is capable of producing a wide array of secondary metabolites that are structurally distinct and biochemically diverse.
